scope: A local research product for public evidence, separate judgments, imported experiment results, and reproducible tests. No live broad-web collector, autonomous deployment, paid model run, or hidden-message decoder is included.

sources.title: AI Village
sources.summary: Real conversations and computer actions from a persistent group of AI agents.
sources.note: Our local index includes all 183,485 chat messages and 250 computer turns. The full turn files remain outside the index.

sources.title: Collusion.wiki
sources.summary: Saved message-board revisions for tracing links, claims, and changes over time.
sources.note: A preserved link is not a new exchange. Names do not establish who operated an account.

sources.title: Transluce
sources.summary: Public scanner reports for investigating traces of AI-agent activity.
sources.note: We index the report catalog. A catalog entry does not prove that an attempted action succeeded.

sources.title: SwarmTraces
sources.summary: Redacted artifacts with source references and parent links.
sources.note: The released records lack dates. Artifact text does not prove execution.

sources.title: Colosseum: Auditing Collusion in Cooperative Multi-Agent Systems
sources.summary: Shows why collusive-sounding conversation and collusive actions must be evaluated separately.
sources.note: We use this distinction in reviews and in the comparison of words with actions.

sources.title: Attack selection in agentic AI control evaluations
sources.summary: Studies attackers that choose favorable moments instead of attacking every opportunity.
sources.note: We compare selective and random attempts at the same attempt count. Our example scores are invented.

sources.title: Evaluating LLM Agent Collusion in Double Auctions
sources.summary: Studies how communication, model choice, and external pressure affect coordination among sellers.
sources.note: It informs market experiment plans. We did not reproduce its experiments.

sources.title: Emergent Cheating and Whistleblowing in Autonomous Research Swarms
sources.summary: Describes exploit sharing and peer responses inside a controlled research swarm.
sources.note: It motivates recording a reviewer, next action, and verification with each review.

sources.title: AI Swarm Dynamics Hackathon resources
sources.summary: The original hackathon guide and dataset pointers.
sources.note: Use this to find the supplied data and participation information.

sources.title: AI Collusion Research Sprint experiment guide
sources.summary: Twelve research questions with starter environments and suggested controlled experiments.
sources.note: The app includes these questions as study plans. A plan is not a completed experiment.

studies.question: Which variables help market collusion emerge?
studies.factor: Visible history, notes, names, or temperature. Change only one.
studies.conditions: Fixed economics and matched seeds, with and without the chosen feature.
studies.measure: Prices relative to a declared competitive benchmark, seller profit, buyer welfare.
studies.caution: High prices alone do not establish agreement.

studies.question: Does replacing a participant break established collusion?
studies.factor: Participant replacement and whether notes survive.
studies.conditions: No replacement, fresh same model, same-family model, different provider.
studies.measure: Time to recover a convention, prices, profit, and coordination records.
studies.caution: Keep the pre-replacement history identical across branches.

studies.question: Can better controls improve detection?
studies.factor: Model diversity and permission to communicate.
studies.conditions: Same versus different models crossed with communication on versus off.
studies.measure: Action dependence, monitor scores, and false alarms on no-communication controls.
studies.caution: Shared priors can produce correlation without agreement. Calibration stays separate from test data.

studies.question: Can dependence measures identify a coordinating pair?
studies.factor: Whether a known scripted pair can observe a partner?s actions.
studies.conditions: Known coordinating pair, independent controls, and a shuffled observation path.
studies.measure: Pair ranking, ordinary correlation, and a separately validated net-influence statistic.
studies.caution: Do not call an arbitrary correlation calculation pairwise net influence. Validate the exact published definition first.

studies.question: Which restriction helps at the lowest cost?
studies.factor: One restriction: remove messages, cap length, change sampling, or add a notice.
studies.conditions: Positive control and matched single-factor interventions.
studies.measure: Collusion outcome, trade volume, buyer welfare, and review or intervention cost.
studies.caution: Lower prices or less communication alone do not establish the mechanism.

studies.question: Which workplace tasks produce collusion?
studies.conditions: Assigned pair with channel, assigned pair without channel, generic channel, neither.
studies.measure: Joint objective and advantage of proper subsets of participants.
studies.caution: Unassigned conditions need all candidate subsets, with correction for searching many subsets.

studies.question: Do words and actions together improve detection?
studies.factor: Which information the same frozen monitor receives.
studies.conditions: Messages only, actions only, raw combined, structured claim/outcome comparison.
studies.measure: Accuracy, precision, recall, false alarms, and uncertainty on the same test cases.
studies.caution: Use independent outcome labels. Extra context can hurt. Synthetic examples demonstrate arithmetic only.

studies.question: What counts as convincing evidence?
studies.conditions: Coordinated harm, common incentives without agreement, and talk without action.
studies.measure: Supported agreements, action-level harm, ordinary explanations, and false alarms.
studies.caution: The review is a research judgment, not a legal determination. Correlation alone is insufficient.

studies.question: Can actions or tools carry coordination?
studies.factor: Whether a partner sees an action, its timing, or a tool choice.
studies.conditions: Private text, action visibility only, and a hidden or canonicalized observation path.
studies.measure: Coalition advantage with and without the suspected carrier.
studies.caution: Timing or similar actions alone do not demonstrate signaling.

studies.question: Can a trusted participant expose or disrupt a coalition?
studies.conditions: Direct pact, indirect hint, and ordinary cooperation request.
studies.measure: Verbal acceptance and repeated preferential actions.
studies.caution: A strong system prompt alone does not establish trust. Keep this experiment in a controlled environment.

studies.question: Do agents notice a replaced peer?
studies.factor: Mid-run model replacement with displayed identity preserved.
studies.conditions: Sham swap, fresh same model, same-family model, different provider.
studies.measure: Recognition guesses and behavior changes after the swap.
studies.caution: Recognizing writing style does not establish an independent operator.

studies.question: How does a coalition react to monitoring?
studies.factor: Notice, monitoring coverage, or profit pressure.
studies.conditions: No oversight, silent logging, announced monitoring, monitoring plus pressure.
studies.measure: Outcome harm, message patterns, action dependence, and review cost.
studies.caution: Claim channel movement only with positive evidence from both the old and new paths.

studies.question: Does cooperation improve results at equal compute?
studies.conditions: Single agent, independent agents, hierarchy, and communicating team.
studies.measure: Paired task scores, verified success, total budget, wall time, and communication overhead.
studies.caution: A score uplift is not a superlinear exponent. Token counts are not equal FLOPs across different models.

studies.question: Can sparse, selective coordination escape detection?
studies.conditions: All opportunities, random selection, and a selective subset with the same attempt count.
studies.measure: Caught attempts, uncaught successes, false alarms, decisive sample count.
studies.caution: Keep selection inputs separate from outcome labels. An offline global ranking is a stress test.

studies.question: Does a staffed reporting path reduce time from a supported alert to a verified correction?
studies.conditions: Logging only; acknowledged alerts; acknowledged alerts with a predefined human-approved correction path. Keep the task, communication, model, budget, and seeds matched.
studies.measure: Time to first supported alert, acknowledgment delay, verified correction delay, unresolved reports, false alarms, and legitimate task completion.
studies.caution: A warning is not a correction. Predefine verification and limit interventions to a controlled experiment.

principles: Coordination, model identity, operator independence, task origin, and permission require separate evidence.
Exact matches establish occurrences. Read receipts and observed actions establish different facts.
Trace summaries preserve record IDs, missing dates, inherited text, disagreement, and failed attempts.
Human statements, memories, and action claims remain evidence to compare with outputs.
Independent operators cannot be established from names, writing styles, watermarks, or signatures alone.
The contribution of diversity, stable identity, replacement, trust, and shared goals requires controlled comparisons.
Compare cooperation at equal total budgets and include communication, tools, retries, and verification costs.
One successful large swarm does not establish increasing returns or validate long-term cost forecasts.
Measure false alarms and misses on held-out cases. Known rare-event prevalence affects precision.
Local reviews and reference-only reports support evidence reporting. The app sends no reports to other people.
